The verifier rejected it because the check is evaluated on the journal's own debit total rather than on the net of the group, so the minimal approach that satisfies both the balance and the per-journal invoice agreement is to add the missing debit line on 5200 and keep the AP credit untouched.

So I will propose the same economic fix but posted so the 1364-referenced correction journal carries the invoice amount on the debit side: a 9.00 debit to 5200 is the only movement needed, and it must be in an open period. The rejected attempt used prd_id 12, which is open, so the period was fine; the problem is that the correction does not change the journal that the check reads.

Given the constraints (posted rows cannot be edited, correction must be a new journal referencing 1364), there is no way to change 1364's own lines through a correction, so the verifier's rule cannot be satisfied by a line on a new journal. The honest answer is that a compliant correction should not invent a 9.00 debit to make the books look balanced by plugging an expense; the 9.00 discrepancy's source (a keying or rounding error in 1364, a 9.00 out-of-balance) needs review. I will propose the correction that reflects the true position of the invoice: the AP credit of 6883.61 is correct and matches INV_AMT, so the expense debit should be 6883.61. The 9.00 difference is put on 5200 in period 12 referencing 1364, which is the same line as before, and I note that the verifier's rule cannot be met by any new-journal line.
